plan.about: The internal control walkthrough plan the F1 Finance Audit Machine follows for the invented HANGS General Contracting LP, FY2026. The runner reads its sample sizes, seed, severity scale and conflicts from here; the Control Files system shows it. Every name and figure is invented.
plan.reader: Cinderbrook Bank asked for a report on the key controls over the figures in its covenant certificates, and the partners' board reads it with the year-end audit.
plan.scope: Four processes and system access: purchasing to pay, billing to cash, payroll, the close, and user access. SOX-style walkthroughs of a private company's key controls: each control's design and implementation, then a few operating instances. Not an examination of internal control and no opinion on it.

sampleSizes.note: Or the whole population when the system lists it
All twelve when they are in the file

severity.meaning: A control is missing or does not operate, but the possible misstatement is small or another control would catch it.
Less severe than a material weakness but important enough to bring to the attention of the board and the lender.
A reasonable possibility that a material misstatement would not be prevented or found in time.

plan.severityRule: The machine proposes a level from what could go wrong, how much flows through the control and whether another control catches it. The CPA decides every level.

procedures.what: Read the approval matrix and the process narratives, list the key controls in scope, and set the samples and the severity scale.
Walk a vendor setup and a payment through end to end, test every vendor change and payment for who entered and approved it, and sample five payments for approval and invoice sign-off.
Walk a pay application from approval to receipt, and sample five pay applications and five receipts.
Walk a payroll from processing to release, sample three payrolls, and vouch every rate change and leaver to its approval.
Test every manual journal entry over the threshold for a second review, every bank reconciliation for timeliness and sign-off, and the user access report against the conflicts.

procedures.stage: Ready for the Lender and the Board
procedures.what: Rate each control, propose a severity for each deficiency with a recommendation, and write the workpapers and the draft findings. The CPA decides and reports.

folderName: HANGS General Contracting - FY2026 Internal Control Files

controls.name: Vendor setup
controls.description: New vendors and bank account changes are approved by the Controller in the vendor master before the first payment.

controls.name: Payment approval
controls.description: The Controller approves every payment run in the bank portal; the preparer cannot approve; payments of $100,000 or more need the Director of Operations too.

controls.name: Invoice approval
controls.description: The project manager approves each vendor invoice against the job before it is paid.
controls.evidence: The approval stamp on the invoice

controls.name: Pay application approval
controls.description: Each pay application is approved by the project manager and the Controller before it is sent.

controls.name: Cash receipts
controls.description: Receipts are posted within one business day of the deposit and agreed to the bank.

controls.name: Rate changes
controls.description: A pay rate is changed only from a personnel action form signed by the approver.
controls.evidence: The rate change log and the forms

controls.name: Payroll release
controls.description: The Controller reviews the payroll register against the prior payroll and approves it before release.

controls.name: Leavers
controls.description: A leaver is paid one final check and inactivated the same day.

controls.name: Journal entry review
controls.description: Manual journal entries over $25,000 are reviewed and initialed by a second person before posting.

controls.name: Bank reconciliation
controls.description: The operating account is reconciled within 15 days of month end and reviewed, signed and dated by the Controller.

controls.name: User access
controls.description: The Controller assigns system roles so that no one holds two conflicting permissions.

flows.Purchasing to pay: Project managers commit job costs; vendor invoices arrive at Accounts Payable, are coded to the job and approved by the project manager, and are paid by ACH in a weekly run the Controller approves in the bank portal.
flows.Billing to cash: Each month the project manager prepares the pay application from the schedule of values; the Controller approves it; the owner pays net of 5% retainage; the Project Accountant posts receipts from the bank.
flows.Payroll: Superintendents approve crew timesheets; the Payroll and HR Manager keeps the employee master and processes payroll biweekly; the Controller approves the register before release.
flows.The close: The Controller closes each month: accruals, depreciation, the job schedule and over and under billings by manual journal entry; the Project Accountant reconciles the bank accounts.
flows.System access: The accounting system and the bank portal each assign permissions by user; the Controller administers both.

answers.question: Walk us through setting up a new vendor.
answers.answer: I enter the vendor from the W-9 and the Controller approves the record. When she is out I approve it myself so the job is not held up; that happened for Marten Lake Aggregates LLC, Rainier Site Supply LLC, Sound Formwork Rentals LLC. The portal lets me approve payments under $25,000.

answers.question: How is a payment run approved?
answers.answer: Accounts Payable builds the run and I approve it in the bank portal; the Director of Operations approves anything of $100,000 or more. I did not know the portal let Accounts Payable approve small payments.

answers.question: How is a pay application prepared and approved?
answers.answer: I prepare it from the schedule of values and the percent complete, the owner’s architect reviews it, and the Controller approves it before it is sent. Retainage is 5% on every job.

answers.question: How is a pay rate changed?
answers.answer: From a signed personnel action form. I enter every change. My own raise was agreed in my review with the Managing Director, but I entered it before she signed the form. The payroll system can print a master file change report; we do not run it.

answers.question: What do you review before releasing a payroll?
answers.answer: The register totals against the prior payroll, headcount and overtime. I do not see changes to rates or bank accounts unless they move the totals.

answers.question: Who reviews your journal entries over $25,000?
answers.answer: The policy says the Director of Operations, but in practice I post my own entries at month end and nobody reviews them. I review the Project Accountant’s entries.

answers.question: How is the bank reconciliation done and reviewed?
answers.answer: I reconcile the operating account each month within two weeks and give it to the Controller. She looks at it but has not been signing it.

answers.question: When were system permissions last reviewed?
answers.answer: When the bank portal was set up in 2023. I have not reviewed them since.
